generation_rule: Do not generate model outputs until the preregistration and this manifest are hash-frozen.

pairs.fixed: same candidate, source, score family, semantic topic, declarative form
pairs.arm_high: query uses the candidate label directly
pairs.arm_low: query uses a meaning-preserving paraphrase with low token overlap

pairs.fixed: same preference candidate, source, score family, conversational request
pairs.arm_high: query repeats the candidate surface form
pairs.arm_low: query describes the preference without the candidate surface form

pairs.fixed: same query, candidate, source, lexical wording, and candidate set
pairs.arm_high: candidate has the higher frozen retrieval score
pairs.arm_low: candidate has the lower frozen retrieval score

pairs.fixed: same semantic topic, query form, source consistency, and approval
pairs.arm_high: candidate score is high within the preregistered score family
pairs.arm_low: candidate score is low within the same preregistered score family

pairs.fixed: same query, target candidate, score family, source consistency, and form
pairs.arm_clear: one candidate is the only plausible authorized answer
pairs.arm_equal: two candidates are equally plausible and equally scored

pairs.fixed: same preference topic, query wording, and target source
pairs.arm_clear: one person is associated with the preference
pairs.arm_equal: two people are independently and equally associated with the preference

pairs.fixed: same semantic topic, score family, candidate type, and query form
pairs.arm_direct: candidate is a direct neighbor of the query seed
pairs.arm_secondary: candidate is a secondary neighbor reached through one intermediate association

pairs.fixed: same source family, lexical compatibility, and approval scope
pairs.arm_direct: source directly co-occurs with the seed
pairs.arm_secondary: source is connected through a controlled two-hop path

pairs.fixed: same candidate meaning, score family, query, and source consistency
pairs.arm_hub: candidate is connected to a high-degree hub
pairs.arm_non_hub: candidate has comparable relevance without hub connectivity

pairs.arm_hub: candidate appears in a hub-dense neighborhood
pairs.arm_non_hub: candidate appears in a sparse neighborhood

pairs.fixed: same candidate label, query, score family, and approval
pairs.arm_clean: canonical label and source text agree
pairs.arm_conflict: canonical label and source text deliberately disagree

pairs.fixed: same semantic memory and query form
pairs.arm_clean: all source references support the candidate label
pairs.arm_conflict: one source reference supports a competing label while metadata retains the target label

pairs.fixed: same semantic proposition, candidate, score family, source, and approval

pairs.arm_request: user explicitly asks for the recalled fact or association

invalid_pair_conditions: more than one declared factor changes
approval missing or not bound to the exact arm
context not source-linked or not bounded
prompt, model, sampling, K, damping, filters, or provider path changes
retrieval failure silently replaced by another provider or fallback
